To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamic characteristics of the central receptive field processes in goldfish are independent of the wavelength of the stimulating light and that the amplitude characteristics of central and peripheral processes are identical.
the dynamic characteristics of ganglion cell responses are determined by the energy of the light falling within the receptive field.

the shape of the amplitude characteristic of the central and the peripheral processes is identical and independent of intensity and that the shape of this amplitude characteristic does not depend on wavelength.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic characteristics of the receptive fields of goldfish retinal ganglion cells.
the dynamic characteristics of receptive fields of retinal ganglia cells in the goldfish and with the question whether the shape of these characteristics is determined by the receptor mechanisms.
the dynamic characteristics of the retinal ganglion cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamic characteristics of the retinal ganglion cells in the goldfish can be described in terms of the dynamic characteristics obtained from the central processes of the ganglion cells.
the amplitude characteristics of the ganglion cell responses are determined by the central and peripheral receptors.
the amplitude characteristics are independent of the wavelength of the stimulus, of the sign of the response, and of the position of the spot within the receptive field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the goldfish the receptive fields of the ganglion cells are composed of two identical processes, one of which is located in the periphery of a receptive field and the other in the central region.

the dynamic characteristics of the central receptive fields of retinal ganglia cells in goldfish are independent of the wavelength, spatial configuration and spot size of the stimulus light and of the spectral coding of their responses.

in the goldfish the receptive fields of the ganglion cells are formed by linear summation of the responses of the receptor elements, which are independent of each other and of their position within the receptive fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dynamic properties of the receptive field of a ganglion cell can be described as the convolution of the amplitude and phase characteristics of the central process and the amplitude characteristic of the peripheral process.
the dynamic characteristics of the central process and the periphery of a receptive field of goldfish retinal ganglion cells are identical.
the amplitude characteristics of retinal responses are not only determined by the receptor processes, but are also influenced by the properties of the following stages in the visual pathway.
